blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements for Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector. To see scheduled maintenance updates for your cloud, visit the Trust Portal.

blocks.heading: Update to Zscaler Cloud Connector Microsoft Azure Instance Type

blocks.text: The Microsoft Azure VM instance type for Zscaler Cloud Connector has been updated to Standard D2ds v5.
To learn more, see Deploying Zscaler Cloud Connector with Microsoft Azure.

blocks.heading: Unified RBAC for Cloud & Branch Connector

blocks.text: Cloud & Branch Connector supports Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Administrators can now view, create, and manage Cloud & Branch Connector roles centrally on the Role Management page (Administration > Role Management).
See image.
The existing Cloud & Branch Connector Role Management page is deprecated if you use Unified RBAC.
To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To learn more, see:
Zscaler Cloud Connector supports the VDI Provisioning permission when adding admin roles. You can select Full, View Only, or None to apply permissions to an admin role.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Admin Roles.

blocks.heading: Zscaler Zero Trust Gateways in Google Cloud Platform

blocks.text: Zscaler has introduced a fully managed, cloud native SaaS security offering in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) that allows you to secure your workload traffic and eliminate the need to manage your security infrastructure in your GCP environment. It provides the same security controls for cloud-to-internet and cloud-to-cloud communication.

To learn more, see What Are Zero Trust Gateways?, About Google Cloud Platform Zero Trust Gateways, Adding a Google Cloud Platform Zero Trust Gateway, Analyzing Google Cloud Platform Zero Trust Gateway Details, and Supported Regions for Zero Trust Gateways.

blocks.heading: Amazon Web Services Support in Zscaler Client Connector for VDI

blocks.text: Support for Amazon Web Services (AWS), Citrix, and Windows servers in AWS using Zscaler Client Connector for VDI is available for Cloud Connector.
To learn more, see What Is Zscaler Client Connector for VDI? and Customizing Zscaler Client Connector for VDI with Install Options for MSI.

New endpoints are added to extend programmatic access to features and functionalities for Zero Trust Gateways (ZTGWs). The following endpoints allow you to create or update ZTGWs. You can also retrieve the ZTGWs, configuration status, number of ZTGWs per organization, list of events that occurred on each ZTGW, license details, etc.:
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference Guide.

blocks.heading: L4 Ingress Support for Cloud & Branch Connector

blocks.text: Cloud & Branch Connector provides Source Network Address Translation (SNAT) and Destination Network Address Translation (DNAT) capabilities in AWS, Azure, and GCP. To learn more, see About Traffic Forwarding and Configuring Traffic Forwarding Rules.
Cloud & Branch Connector supports Azure Gateway Load Balancer via Terraform.

blocks.heading: Supported Regions for Zscaler Zero Trust Gateways

blocks.text: Zscaler Zero Trust Gateways are available in the ap-south-2 and ap-southeast-4 Amazon Web Services (AWS) regions.
To learn more, see Supported Regions for Zero Trust Gateways.

Zscaler Cloud Connector supports enhanced upgrade capabilities by allowing you to select release channels. When upgrading your Cloud Connectors, you can choose between the stable, latest, or beta release channels.
See image.
To learn more, see About Upgrade Manager, Managing Cloud & Branch Connector Upgrades, About Cloud Connector Groups, Editing Cloud Connectors, and Configuring a Cloud Provisioning Template.

New endpoints are added to extend programmatic access for managing Cloud & Branch Connector virtual machines (VMs). The following APIs allow you to update the release channel for VMs, update the status of VMs in bulk, and retrieve the release channel and scheduled upgrade metrics:
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference Guide.

blocks.heading: Update to Zscaler Cloud Connector Microsoft Azure Virtual Machine in China

blocks.text: The Microsoft Azure VM image for Zscaler Cloud Connector in China has been updated to version 42.1.0. This image contains OS security fixes and certificate updates. Zscaler recommends that all new deployments utilize the latest image.
To learn more, see Deploying Zscaler Cloud Connector with Microsoft Azure, Deployment Templates for Zscaler Cloud Connector, and Identifying the Zscaler Cloud Connector Version.

blocks.heading: Update to Zscaler Cloud Connector Amazon Machine Image

blocks.text: The AMI for Zscaler Cloud Connector has been updated to version ZS42.1.0. This image contains OS security fixes and certificate updates. Zscaler recommends that all new deployments utilize the latest image. Ensure that you refresh all Infrastructure as Code (IaC) deployment templates to use the latest image. Also, autoscaling-based deployments must have their launch template versions updated to select these new AMI IDs for scale-outs.
To learn more, see Deploying Zscaler Cloud Connector with Amazon Web Services, Deployment Templates for Zscaler Cloud Connector, and Identifying the Zscaler Cloud Connector Version.

blocks.heading: Update to Zscaler Cloud Connector Google Cloud Platform Virtual Machine

blocks.text: The Google Cloud Platform (GCP) VM image for Zscaler Cloud Connector has been updated to version zs-cc-ga-03092026. This image contains OS security fixes and certificate updates. Zscaler recommends that all new deployments utilize the latest image. Use the latest GCP Terraform scripts (v0.3.1) that default to the new Google Cloud Marketplace image.
To learn more, see Deploying Zscaler Cloud Connector on the Google Cloud Platform, Deployment Templates for Zscaler Cloud Connector, and Identifying the Zscaler Cloud Connector Version.

blocks.heading: Update to Zscaler Cloud Connector Microsoft Azure Virtual Machine

blocks.text: The Microsoft Azure VM image for Zscaler Cloud Connector has been updated to version 42.1.0. This image contains OS security fixes and certificate updates. Zscaler recommends that all new deployments utilize the latest image.
To learn more, see Deploying Zscaler Cloud Connector with Microsoft Azure, Deployment Templates for Zscaler Cloud Connector, and Identifying the Zscaler Cloud Connector Version.

New endpoints are added to extend programmatic access to features and functionalities for Azure accounts and groups. The following endpoints allow you to create, update, and delete Azure accounts and account groups. You can also retrieve the list of available Azure accounts, Cloud Connector groups for the specified regions, total number of Azure accounts, etc.:
To learn more about each endpoint, see the API Reference Guide.

blocks.heading: Cloud & Branch Connector Monitoring Dashboard Enhancements

blocks.text: The Cloud & Branch Connector Monitoring page has improved data about your total entitled and deployed Cloud & Branch Connector devices.
See image.
To learn more, see Accessing Cloud & Branch Connector Monitoring, Analyzing Cloud Connector Details, and Analyzing Branch Connector Details.

blocks.heading: Increased Number of Subscriptions per Azure Partner Integrations Account

blocks.text: The maximum number of subscriptions under a Cloud Connector Azure partner integrations account increased from 32 to 128.
To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations and About Microsoft Azure Accounts.

blocks.heading: Supported Regions for Zscaler Zero Trust Gateways

blocks.text: Zscaler Zero Trust Gateways are available in the me-south-1, eu-north-1, and eu-south-2 Amazon Web Services (AWS) regions.
To learn more, see Analyzing Zero Trust Gateway Details.

blocks.heading: Support for AWS Endpoint ID in Session Insights Logs

blocks.text: Zscaler Cloud Connector supports the Endpoint/Interface filter and column in the Session Insights Logs, which is the Amazon Web Services (AWS) virtual private cloud (VPC) endpoint ID that connects to the Gateway Load Balancer.
To learn more, see Session Insights Logs: Columns and Session Insights Logs: Filters.

blocks.heading: ZPA Pattern Matching for Cloud Connector

blocks.text: Cloud Connector supports ZPA pattern matching. Admins can define applications with patterns within application segments. Pattern matching allows you to use the policy evaluation with hostname patterns instead of exact FQDNs.
To learn more, see Using Pattern Matching for Application Segments.

blocks.heading: Zscaler Client Connector for VDI Username Visibility

blocks.text: When logged in to multisession Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI), you can view your username using the Zscaler Client Connector for VDI application.
See image.
To learn more, see What Is Zscaler Client Connector for VDI?

blocks.heading: Cloud Connector MIG Autoscaling with Google Cloud Platform

blocks.text: A new version of the Zscaler Cloud Connector Google Cloud Platform (GCP) virtual machine (VM) is available. Version zs-cc-ga-02042026 supports a Managed Instance Group (MIG) with autoscaling deployment with GCP. In the Zscaler Cloud & Branch Connector Admin Portal, references to autoscaling also refer to a MIG with autoscaling. To enable autoscaling, contact Zscaler Support.

To learn more, see Understanding Cloud Connector Deployments with Google Cloud Platform Managed Instance Groups with Autoscaling, Deploying Zscaler Cloud Connector on the Google Cloud Platform, Deployment Templates for Zscaler Cloud Connector, About Cloud Connector Groups, About Cloud Provisioning Templates, and Configuring a Cloud Provisioning Template.
